claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings are used as protective coatings on zirconium-alloy fuel cladding.
A standard Cr coating on zirconium alloy suffers premature failure under elevated-temperature conditions.
Premature failure of the standard Cr coating is caused by Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
The proposed intervention consists of a graded adhesion interlayer, an approximately 20 nm ALD-deposited Al2O3 layer, and an approximately 5 micrometer elemental Cr coating.
The graded interlayer enhances adhesion between the zirconium alloy and the alumina barrier.
The graded interlayer reduces thermal mismatch between the zirconium alloy and the alumina barrier.
Reducing thermal mismatch prevents interfacial crack formation during rapid temperature changes.
ALD produces a dense, conformal Al2O3 diffusion barrier in this coating architecture.
Al2O3 has sufficiently low atomic diffusivity to block Cr and Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
The combined graded interlayer and alumina barrier will maintain barrier integrity under thermal cycling.
The intervention will preserve Cr-coating integrity and protective function during normal subcritical-water operation.
The intervention will preserve Cr-coating integrity and protective function during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
Relevant normal-operation conditions are approximately 320 degrees Celsius and 11.3 MPa in subcritical water.
The protective effect is expected to persist in steam at temperatures up to approximately 1200 degrees Celsius for approximately one hour.
Compared with an unmodified Cr coating, the modified system will develop a substantially thinner Cr-Zr interdiffusion zone.
Compared with an unmodified Cr coating, the modified system will sustain better adhesion after the specified exposures.
Compared with an unmodified Cr coating, the modified system will maintain better oxidation and corrosion protection.
Conventional Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
A significant Cr-Zr interdiffusion zone compromises adhesion and causes earlier failure of the conventional coating.
Long-term robustness under repeated thermal-mechanical cycling remains uncharacterized.
